To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adenylation domains are the substrate-selecting units of NRPS and MbtH proteins are required for their activity.
the adenylation domains and MbtH proteins can be utilized as a tool to discover cryptic gene clusters.

(1) The adenylation domain of the NRPS gene cluster is a substrate selecting domain and (2) the presence of putative domain and Mbt homologs in the genome helps to identify novel secondary metabolite producing bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel secondary metabolites by in silico analysis of microbial genomes, and their characterization by bioinformatic, genetic and biochemical tools.
the identification of novel cryptic gene clusters of NRPS/PKS in sequenced genomes and the in silico prediction of their novel products.
the identification and characterization of cryptic NRPSs, their gene clusters and the decoding of the natural product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenylation domains are the key to the NRPS gene cluster identification, which in turn is the key to novel natural product discovery.
NRPSs are a promising source of novel natural products and the identification of cryptic NRPS clusters is an emerging field of research.
the identification of the cryptic gene cluster is a prerequisite for the production of the novel NRPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adenylation domains are the best tools to screen the genome and identify the NRPS gene cluster, which is the key step to identify the novel secondary metabolic products.
the adenylation domains are the most promising tools in the identification of novel cryptic gene clusters, thus opening up the possibility of discovering novel secondary metabolites.
the NRPS adenylation domains are the key players for identifying the cryptic gene cluster and thus decoding the novel NRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of the adenylyl domain and Mbt homologs can be used as a powerful tool to screen the genome for the cryptic NRPS clusters.
the identification of novel cryptic gene clusters in the sequenced microbial genomes can be achieved using the adenylation domains and their associated proteins as tools.
the presence of a putative adenylication domain and Mbt H homolog in the genome can help identify novel secondary metabolite producing microorganisms.
